newsitem.title: CHINA: China seizes contaminated soybeans from Japan.
newsitem.headline: China seizes contaminated soybeans from Japan.

text.p: Chinese officials have seized a parcel of soybean seeds from Japan that was contaminated by a dangerous fungus, a quarantine official said on Tuesday.
"The fungus is very dangerous to soybeans," an official of the State Bureau of Animals and Plants Quarantine said by telephone.

Officials of the the Beijing Bureau of Animals and Plants Quarantine confiscated the parcel at the city's international post exchange centre earlier this month. It had been mailed from Japan to a unit in Beijing, he said.
The fungus could cut soybean output by half, or as much as 75 percent in some extreme cases, he said. It could also cut output of other crops, such as kidney beans and peas.
It was the first time China had discovered this fungus on imported soybeans, the official said, but gave no further details.
